description: ValidatedPath is marked #[non_exhaustive] (line 250) but has all-public fields. non_exhaustive prevents external callers from struct-initializing it or pattern-matching exhaustively, which is the right choice for a library type. However with public fields, callers can still read anchor_index and depth directly. This is actually fine and intentional, but the crate has no doc comment explaining why fields are pub despite non_exhaustive. Without explanation, maintainers may wonder if the public fields were a mistake. Add a doc comment clarifying that non_exhaustive guards against future field additions without breaking match syntax, while pub fields allow read access.
title: ValidatedPath pub fields and non_exhaustive together inconsistent
